subject: Linguistics
title: Turn-Taking in Conversation
description: A quick, practical guide to Turn-Taking in Conversation.

hook.text: Two people rarely talk at the same time—yet there's no traffic light. How do turns work?

buildup.text: Sacks, Schegloff, and Jefferson described the turn-taking system in 1974.

discovery.text: Speakers signal turn completion through intonation, syntax, and gaze—listeners time their entry.

twist.text: The gap between turns averages just 200 milliseconds—listeners must plan while still listening.

climax.text: This system works across all studied languages—it's a universal of human conversation.

punchline.text: Conversation is precision timing disguised as casual chat.

quiz.question: How long is the average gap between conversational turns?
